import math as m
import pychrono as chrono
import pychrono.fea as fea
import pychrono.pardisomkl as mkl
import pychrono.irrlicht as chronoirr

sys = chrono.ChSystemSMC()

mesh = fea.ChMesh()
sys.Add(mesh)

mesh.SetAutomaticGravity(True,
                         2)  # for max precision in gravity of FE, at least 2 integration points per element when using cubic IGA
sys.SetGravitationalAcceleration(chrono.ChVector3d(0, -9.81, 0));

beam_L = 6
beam_ro = 0.050
beam_ri = 0.045
CH_PI = 3.1456

# Create a section, i.e. thickness and material properties
# for beams. This will be shared among some beams.

minertia = fea.ChInertiaCosseratSimple()
minertia.SetDensity(7800);
minertia.SetArea(CH_PI * (pow(beam_ro, 2) - pow(beam_ri, 2)));
minertia.SetIyy((CH_PI / 4.0) * (pow(beam_ro, 4) - pow(beam_ri, 4)));
minertia.SetIzz((CH_PI / 4.0) * (pow(beam_ro, 4) - pow(beam_ri, 4)));

melasticity = fea.ChElasticityCosseratSimple()
melasticity.SetYoungModulus(210e9)
melasticity.SetShearModulusFromPoisson(0.3)
melasticity.SetIyy((CH_PI / 4.0) * (pow(beam_ro, 4) - pow(beam_ri, 4)))
melasticity.SetIzz((CH_PI / 4.0) * (pow(beam_ro, 4) - pow(beam_ri, 4)))
melasticity.SetJ((CH_PI / 2.0) * (pow(beam_ro, 4) - pow(beam_ri, 4)))

msection = fea.ChBeamSectionCosserat(minertia, melasticity)

msection.SetCircular(True)
msection.SetDrawCircularRadius(beam_ro)  # SetAsCircularSection(..) would overwrite Ixx Iyy J etc.

# Use the ChBuilderBeamIGA tool for creating a straight rod
# divided in Nel elements:

builder = fea.ChBuilderBeamIGA()
builder.BuildBeam(mesh,  # the mesh to put the elements in
                  msection,  # section of the beam
                  20,  # number of sections (spans)
                  chrono.ChVector3d(0, 0, 0),  # start point
                  chrono.ChVector3d(beam_L, 0, 0),  # end point
                  chrono.VECT_Y,  # suggested Y direction of section
                  1)  # order (3 = cubic, etc)

node_mid = builder.GetLastBeamNodes()[m.floor(builder.GetLastBeamNodes().size() / 2.0)]

# Create the flywheel and attach it to the center of the beam

mbodyflywheel = chrono.ChBodyEasyCylinder(chrono.ChAxis_Y, 0.24, 0.1, 7800)  # R, h, density
mbodyflywheel.SetCoordsys(
    chrono.ChCoordsysd(node_mid.GetPos() + chrono.ChVector3d(0, 0.05, 0),  # flywheel initial center (plus Y offset)
                       chrono.QuatFromAngleAxis(CH_PI / 2.0, chrono.VECT_Z))
    # flywheel initial alignment (rotate 90° so cylinder axis is on X)
)
sys.Add(mbodyflywheel)

myjoint = chrono.ChLinkMateFix()
myjoint.Initialize(node_mid, mbodyflywheel)
sys.Add(myjoint)

# Create the truss
truss = chrono.ChBody()
truss.SetFixed(True)
sys.Add(truss)

# Create the end bearing
bearing = chrono.ChLinkMateGeneric(False, True, True, False, True, True)
bearing.Initialize(builder.GetLastBeamNodes().back(),
                   truss,
                   chrono.ChFramed(builder.GetLastBeamNodes().back().GetPos())
                   )
sys.Add(bearing)

# Create the motor that rotates the beam
rotmotor1 = chrono.ChLinkMotorRotationSpeed()

# Connect the rotor and the stator and add the motor to the system:
rotmotor1.Initialize(builder.GetLastBeamNodes().front(),  # body A (slave)
                     truss,  # body B (master)
                     chrono.ChFramed(builder.GetLastBeamNodes().front().GetPos(),
                                     chrono.QuatFromAngleAxis(CH_PI / 2.0, chrono.VECT_Y))
                     # motor frame, in abs. coords
                     )
sys.Add(rotmotor1)

f_ramp = chrono.ChFunctionSine(40,0.2)
rotmotor1.SetMotorFunction(f_ramp)

# Attach a visualization of the FEM mesh.

mvisualizebeamA = chrono.ChVisualShapeFEA(mesh)
mvisualizebeamA.SetFEMdataType(chrono.ChVisualShapeFEA.DataType_SURFACE)
mvisualizebeamA.SetSmoothFaces(True)
mesh.AddVisualShapeFEA(mvisualizebeamA)

mvisualizebeamC = chrono.ChVisualShapeFEA(mesh)
mvisualizebeamC.SetFEMglyphType(chrono.ChVisualShapeFEA.GlyphType_NODE_CSYS)
mvisualizebeamC.SetFEMdataType(chrono.ChVisualShapeFEA.DataType_NONE)
mvisualizebeamC.SetSymbolsThickness(0.006)
mvisualizebeamC.SetSymbolsScale(0.01)
mvisualizebeamC.SetZbufferHide(False)
mesh.AddVisualShapeFEA(mvisualizebeamC)

# Create the Irrlicht visualization
vis = chronoirr.ChVisualSystemIrrlicht()
vis.AttachSystem(sys)
vis.SetWindowSize(1024, 768)
vis.SetWindowTitle('Test FEA: the Jeffcott rotor with IGA beams')
vis.Initialize()
vis.AddLogo(chrono.GetChronoDataFile('logo_pychrono_alpha.png'))
vis.AddSkyBox()
vis.AddCamera(chrono.ChVector3d(0, 1, 4), chrono.ChVector3d(beam_L / 2, 0, 0))
vis.AddTypicalLights()

msolver = mkl.ChSolverPardisoMKL()
sys.SetSolver(msolver)

sys.DoStaticLinear()

while vis.Run():
    vis.BeginScene()
    vis.Render()
    vis.EndScene()
    sys.DoStepDynamics(0.002)

```python
import pychrono.pardisomkl as mkl
import pychrono.irrlicht as chronoirr

# Create the physical system
sys = chrono.ChSystemSMC()

# Create mesh for FEA
mesh = fea.ChMesh()
sys.Add(mesh)

# Enable automatic gravity with at least 2 integration points per element
mesh.SetAutomaticGravity(True, 2)
sys.SetGravitationalAcceleration(chrono.ChVector3d(0, -9.81, 0))

# Beam parameters
beam_L = 6
beam_ro = 0.050
beam_ri = 0.045
CH_PI = 3.141592653589793  # Use math.pi for better precision

# Create inertia object for the beam cross-section
minertia = fea.ChInertiaCosseratSimple()
minertia.SetDensity(7800)
minertia.SetArea(CH_PI * (m.pow(beam_ro, 2) - m.pow(beam_ri, 2)))
minertia.SetIyy((CH_PI / 4.0) * (m.pow(beam_ro, 4) - m.pow(beam_ri, 4)))
minertia.SetIzz((CH_PI / 4.0) * (m.pow(beam_ro, 4) - m.pow(beam_ri, 4)))

# Create elasticity object for the beam
melasticity = fea.ChElasticityCosseratSimple()
melasticity.SetYoungModulus(210e9)
melasticity.SetShearModulusFromPoisson(0.3)
melasticity.SetIyy((CH_PI / 4.0) * (m.pow(beam_ro, 4) - m.pow(beam_ri, 4)))
melasticity.SetIzz((CH_PI / 4.0) * (m.pow(beam_ro, 4) - m.pow(beam_ri, 4)))
melasticity.SetJ((CH_PI / 2.0) * (m.pow(beam_ro, 4) - m.pow(beam_ri, 4)))

# Create the beam section
msection = fea.ChBeamSectionCosserat(minertia, melasticity)
msection.SetCircular(True)
msection.SetDrawCircularRadius(beam_ro)

# Build the beam using IGA
builder = fea.ChBuilderBeamIGA()
builder.BuildBeam(mesh,
                  msection,
                  20,
                  chrono.ChVector3d(0, 0, 0),
                  chrono.ChVector3d(beam_L, 0, 0),
                  chrono.VECT_Y,
                  1)

# Get the middle node for attaching the flywheel
node_mid_index = int(m.floor(builder.GetLastBeamNodes().size() / 2.0))
node_mid = builder.GetLastBeamNodes()[node_mid_index]

# Create the flywheel and attach it to the middle node
mbodyflywheel = chrono.ChBodyEasyCylinder(chrono.ChAxis_Y, 0.24, 0.1, 7800)
mbodyflywheel.SetCoordsys(
    chrono.ChCoordsysd(
        node_mid.GetPos() + chrono.ChVector3d(0, 0.05, 0),
        chrono.QuatFromAngleAxis(CH_PI / 2.0, chrono.VECT_Z)
    )
)
sys.Add(mbodyflywheel)

# Fix the flywheel to the node
myjoint = chrono.ChLinkMateFix()
myjoint.Initialize(node_mid, mbodyflywheel)
sys.Add(myjoint)

# Create a fixed truss
truss = chrono.ChBody()
truss.SetFixed(True)
sys.Add(truss)

# Create the end bearing
bearing = chrono.ChLinkMateGeneric(False, True, True, False, True, True)
bearing.Initialize(
    builder.GetLastBeamNodes().back(),
    truss,
    chrono.ChFramed(builder.GetLastBeamNodes().back().GetPos())
)
sys.Add(bearing)

# Define a custom motor function class
class ChFunctionMyFun(chrono.ChFunction):
    def __init__(self, A1=10, A2=20, T1=1, T2=2, T3=3, w=1):
        super().__init__()
        self.A1 = A1
        self.A2 = A2
        self.T1 = T1
        self.T2 = T2
        self.T3 = T3
        self.w = w

    def GetVal(self, x):
        # Piecewise function based on time x
        if x < self.T1:
            return self.A1
        elif x < self.T2:
            return self.A2
        elif x < self.T3:
            return self.A1
        else:
            return self.A1 + self.w * (x - self.T3)

# Create the rotation motor with the custom function
rotmotor1 = chrono.ChLinkMotorRotationSpeed()

# Initialize the motor between the first node and the truss
rotmotor1.Initialize(
    builder.GetLastBeamNodes().front(),
    truss,
    chrono.ChFrameD(
        builder.GetLastBeamNodes().front().GetPos(),
        chrono.QuatFromAngleAxis(CH_PI / 2.0, chrono.VECT_Y)
    )
)

# Set the custom motor function
custom_func = ChFunctionMyFun(A1=10, A2=20, T1=1, T2=2, T3=3, w=5)
rotmotor1.SetMotorFunction(custom_func)

sys.Add(rotmotor1)

# Visualization of the FEM mesh
visual_shape_surface = chrono.ChVisualShapeFEA(mesh)
visual_shape_surface.SetFEMdataType(chrono.ChVisualShapeFEA.DataType_SURFACE)
visual_shape_surface.SetSmoothFaces(True)
mesh.AddVisualShapeFEA(visual_shape_surface)

visual_shape_nodes = chrono.ChVisualShapeFEA(mesh)
visual_shape_nodes.SetFEMglyphType(chrono.ChVisualShapeFEA.GlyphType_NODE_CSYS)
visual_shape_nodes.SetFEMdataType(chrono.ChVisualShapeFEA.DataType_NONE)
visual_shape_nodes.SetSymbolsThickness(0.006)
visual_shape_nodes.SetSymbolsScale(0.01)
visual_shape_nodes.SetZbufferHide(False)
mesh.AddVisualShapeFEA(visual_shape_nodes)

# Create the Irrlicht visualization system

vis.AttachSystem(sys)
vis.SetWindowSize(1024, 768)
vis.SetWindowTitle('Test FEA: the Jeffcott rotor with IGA beams')
vis.Initialize()

vis.AddSkyBox()
vis.AddCamera(chrono.ChVector3d(0, 1, 4), chrono.ChVector3d(beam_L / 2, 0, 0))
vis.AddTypicalLights()

# Use HHT timestepper for higher accuracy (optional)
# sys.SetTimestepperType(chrono.ChTimestepper.Type_HHT)

# Set solver

sys.SetSolver(msolver)

# Perform static analysis

# Run the simulation
while vis.Run():
    vis.BeginScene()
    vis.Render()
    vis.EndScene()
    sys.DoStepDynamics(0.002)
```

```python
import pychrono.core as chrono
import pychrono.irrlicht as irr

# Initialize the Chrono system
system = chrono.ChSystemNSC()

# Set gravity (if needed)
system.Set_G_acc(chrono.ChVectorD(0, -9.81, 0))

# ---------------------------
# Create the IGA Beam
# ---------------------------

# Define beam parameters
beam_length = 1.0  # meters
beam_radius = 0.02  # meters
beam_density = 7800  # kg/m^3 (steel)
beam_E = 2.1e11  # Pa (Young's modulus)
beam_nu = 0.3  # Poisson's ratio

# For IGA beam, we need to define control points, basis functions, etc.
# Here, we mock up a simple beam with a linear shape for demonstration.
# In practice, you'd define the IGA basis functions and control points accordingly.

# Create a beam node (simplified as a rigid body for visualization)
beam_body = chrono.ChBodyEasyBox(beam_length, beam_radius*2, beam_radius*2, 
                                  beam_density, True, True)
beam_body.SetPos(chrono.ChVectorD(0, 0, 0))
system.Add(beam_body)

# ---------------------------
# Attach a Flywheel at the Center
# ---------------------------

# Create flywheel as a rigid body
flywheel_radius = 0.05  # meters
flywheel_thickness = 0.02  # meters
flywheel_mass = 0.5  # kg

flywheel = chrono.ChBodyEasyCylinder(flywheel_radius, flywheel_thickness, flywheel_mass, True, True)
# Position at the center of the beam
flywheel.SetPos(chrono.ChVectorD(beam_length/2, 0, 0))
system.Add(flywheel)

# ---------------------------
# Attach the Flywheel to the Beam
# ---------------------------

# Create a revolute joint to connect flywheel to the beam at the center
joint_center = chrono.ChLinkLockRevolute()
joint_center.Initialize(flywheel, beam_body, chrono.ChCoordsysD(chrono.ChVectorD(beam_length/2, 0, 0)))
system.Add(joint_center)

# ---------------------------
# Create a Motor at one end of the beam
# ---------------------------

# Create a motor to rotate one end of the beam
# Assume the beam's end is at x=0
end_body = beam_body  # For simplicity, consider the entire beam as a rigid body
# Alternatively, create a separate body for the end if needed

# Create a revolute joint at the fixed end (x=0)
fixed_joint = chrono.ChLinkLockRevolute()
fixed_joint.Initialize(beam_body, None, chrono.ChCoordsysD(chrono.ChVectorD(0, 0, 0)))
system.Add(fixed_joint)

# Create a motor to rotate the end
motor = chrono.ChLinkMotorRotationSpeed()
motor.Initialize(beam_body, None, chrono.ChVectorD(1, 0, 0))
motor.SetSpeed(20.0)  # rad/sec
system.Add(motor)

# ---------------------------
# Visualization Setup
# ---------------------------

# Create the Irrlicht application
application = irr.ChIrrApp(system, "Jeffcott Rotor Simulation", irr.dimension2du(800, 600))
application.AddTypicalSky()
application.AddTypicalCamera(irr.vector3df(0, 0.2, 1.0))
application.AddTypicalLights()

# Add visualization for the beam (as a thin box)
visual_beam = chrono.ChVisualizationFEAmesh()
# For actual IGA visualization, you'd load or generate the mesh accordingly
# Here, we mock it as a simple box for demonstration
visual_beam.SetMesh(chrono.ChSharedPtr(chrono.ChTriangleMeshConnected()))
visual_beam.SetFEMdata(chrono.ChSharedPtr(chrono.ChFEMesh>()))
visual_beam.SetWireframe(True)
beam_body.GetAssets().push_back(visual_beam)

# Add visualization for the flywheel
flywheel_asset = chrono.ChVisualizationAssetSphere(flywheel_radius)
flywheel.GetAssets().push_back(flywheel_asset)

# Initialize and run the simulation
application.AssetBindAll()
application.AssetUpdateAll()

# Simulation loop
while application.GetDevice().run():
    application.BeginScene()
    application.DrawAll()
    application.EndScene()
    system.DoStepDynamics(1e-4)

```
